basis: Marrow failure defines FANCN; thumb hypoplasia 3/8 and microphthalmia 3/7 support involvement. Microcephaly alone lacks functional CNS evidence; associated tumors are separate diseases.

decisions.neurologic: none: microcephaly in 16/18 does not establish functional brain damage; medulloblastoma is a separately diagnosed malignancy.

basis: Hemolysis, thrombocytopenia and renal injury define HUS; complement-mediated immune injury predominates. Intrinsic small-vessel thrombosis/endothelial damage occurs in essentially all.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: intrinsic thrombotic microangiopathy damages small vessels in essentially all; three primary slots retain blood, kidney and immune mechanism.
decisions.infectious_immune: primary: inherited complement dysregulation causes immune-mediated endothelial injury in the predominant hereditary HUS forms.

basis: Osteopetrosis with antibody deficiency; visual loss 8/8; marrow compromise is common (>30%) in malignant osteopetrosis. Hepatomegaly alone does not establish hepatic damage.

decisions.haematologic: involved: marrow encroachment and anemia commonly exceed 30% in malignant osteopetrosis; splenomegaly in 3/8 supports extramedullary hematopoiesis.

basis: Localized immune-complex vasculitis characteristically arises in skin/subcutis, producing tissue inflammation and sometimes necrosis.

decisions.dermatologic: primary: the characteristic lesion is localized cutaneous/subcutaneous immune-complex vasculitis, rather than an incidental transient rash.

basis: Auricular chondritis, arthritis and large-vessel vasculitis each 80-99% per HPO. Airway damage 30-79% and diagnostic ocular inflammation omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: supplied HPO reports destructive large-vessel vasculitis in 80-99%, supporting priority within the four-axis cap.
decisions.pulmonary: none: airway damage qualifies at 30-79%, but is omitted at the cap in favor of more frequent auricular, joint and vascular disease plus the immune mechanism.

basis: Skeletal, hair/nail and dental dysplasia define CED1; CKD in 2/2 assessed supports renal involvement. Hepatic fibrosis and retinal dystrophy each 1/10.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: hypodontia/anodontia and microdontia are characteristic defining ectodermal defects; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.

basis: Tumor originates in the duodenum. Somatostatin expression alone establishes neither an endocrine-gland origin nor a functional endocrine syndrome.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: none: duodenal neuroendocrine-cell origin and somatostatin production alone do not establish endocrine-gland disease or a metabolic disorder.

basis: Glycosylation synthesis disorder; neurodevelopmental impairment affects most. Intrinsic hepatic dysfunction and coagulation-factor deficiencies each commonly exceed 30%, with subtype variability.

decisions.haematologic: involved: intrinsic deficiencies of glycosylated coagulation factors commonly exceed 30% across the predominant type I presentations; clinical thrombosis is not required.
decisions.hepatic: involved: intrinsic hepatopathy/hepatic dysfunction commonly exceeds 30% in predominant type I presentations; isolated transient enzyme elevation is insufficient.

basis: Peripheral neuropathy with established distal muscle wasting in 10-11/15 (67-73%). Macular degeneration 3/14 and skin hyperextensibility 4/14 fall below 30%.

decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: documented amyotrophy in 10-11/15 represents substantial muscle tissue loss intrinsic to the neuropathy, beyond weakness alone.

basis: Intellectual disability and anal atresia (4/5) define FG1; optic nerve hypoplasia and auditory canal stenosis each 30-79%. Broad digits alone do not establish locomotor damage.

decisions.musculoskeletal: none: broad digits and skeletal shape differences do not establish functional locomotor damage; hypotonia is attributable to the neurodevelopmental disorder.
decisions.otologic: involved: external auditory canal stenosis is a structural ear lesion reported in 30-79%; this supports involvement independently of cosmetic pinna differences.
